name: Howl
description: The sound feeds back on itself like an amplifier in the room: held notes bloom into an overtone of the note Distance tunes, and it never runs away.

meters.name: Loop gain a new note took off

params.name: Gain
params.description: How readily it feeds back. Low only rings a little after each note. Past the middle a held note tips over and sings, and the higher it is the sooner it takes over.

params.name: Distance
params.description: How far the sound travels round the loop. It tunes a low note, and the feedback sings only on that note's overtones. Longer is lower, with the overtones closer.

params.name: Body
params.description: The resonance in the loop, which picks the overtone that sings. Low is dark and woody, high is bright and wiry.

params.name: Hold
params.description: How long it sings on after the playing stops. Short lets it fall with each note, long leaves a tone hanging in the room. It always dies away in the end.

params.name: Move
params.description: How far the resonance wanders by itself, as when a player moves at the amplifier. At zero one overtone holds. Higher, the feedback climbs and falls through others.

params.name: Pace
params.description: How fast the resonance wanders when Move is up. Slow drifts from one overtone to the next over many seconds, fast flickers between them.

params.name: Edge
params.description: How rough the singing tone is. At zero it is a pure, round tone. Higher adds a hard, reedy buzz on top of it.

params.name: Follow
params.description: How much the feedback gives way to a new note. At zero it sings straight through the playing. Higher, each attack knocks it back and it blooms again as the note rings.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far apart the left and right loops stand. At zero both sing the same overtone. Higher, each side leans to a different one and wanders by itself.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between your playing and the feedback.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A delay, a resonance and a level hold in a loop, tuned so that the loop sings on the harmonics of the note the delay sets; not a model of any amplifier or pedal.
